newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel chief to support savings tax.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel chief to support savings tax.

text.p: Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel on Wednesday said he will support the Treasury's entire proposal for capital market reform, including a politically sensitive tax on short- and medium-term savings.
Until now Frenkel has opposed the tax, saying he feared it would hurt the savings rate at a time when it is declining.

"In light of the possibility that the report (on capital market reform) might not be implemented in the end, or would be changed so significantly that it would not help the capital markets, I would recommend today to adopt the entire report, including the new taxes with certain adjustments," he said.
He told a seminar the adjustments should include a lowering of the tax on savings of less than 10 years, something the Treasury is already reportedly considering.
Early on Monday, the government delayed a vote on the savings tax, seen as crucial to the whole reform package, so a committee could study the tax over the next two weeks.
The committee is made up of the directors general of the Treasury, Prime Minister's office and the Bank of Israel.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had pushed for the cabinet to delay the vote.
